There's a few weaker bonus attacks that individual party members can do but that's it really. The character growth system in this game is a real disappointment compared to other games in the series. To be frank, there is no thinking involved. An example: Of course one would pick a stronger lightning spell to replace a weaker version of the same spell. There is just no strategy or thought put into this game. It may as well have been done for the player. Story: 1/10 Loved the beginning and then because of poor presentation and terrible characters it ruined itself. You're suppose to be trying to find some killer who is supposedly kidnapping people and throwing them into a harsh world inside televisions but the game makes it completely obvious who the culprit is from the very beginning and continues to be obvious about the killer. They honestly didn't even try in this game. I was very disappointed. I'd go on and on about why it was so obvious but that would be spoilers AND I'd rather not ruin it for people if they haven't already seen the obvious plot. I'll give you a hint though if you think I'm lying: "Confidential." Worst of all, the reasoning was, for all intents and purposes, non-existent. It was little more than "I'm bored" to "I'm crazy because the plot needs me to be some random crazy person now." Characters: 1/10 ALL social links, the character development that the characters express in the game, all end the same. They talk about a particular problem, they exaggerate how bad this problem is, some sob story is given in a one-sided depiction of the specified problem, and then by the end of the social link the character will go on having the problem and say their complaints before were exaggerated and that there is no problem. Nothing really changes for the characters. They don't try to deal with problems but just stop complaining about them. An example? Yukiko Amagi, she shows great strides in trying to get a job and live on her own to support herself and grow-up from being a spoiled brat and then the social link changes to some lunacy about some camera crew for some random tabloid wanting to make a mockery of her parents historical inn (which she didn't want to inherit and instead grow-up and make a life of her own) and then some random workers in the family speak about how they adored Yukiko as a kid, and by the end of it Yukiko defends her crying mother against these people from this random tabloid company with you, the main character's, help as support. Overall, I found the entire experience to be a laughable melodramatic sob story and was completely embarrassed to be playing it. Now, one shouldn't judge an entire system in a game on just one bad egg, right? The problem was, I kept finding this same chain of events in every social link so I just got tired of it. To conclude: If you like Japanese RPGs full of high school drama or liked previous Persona games then this is definitely for you. If you like good rpgs then this game isn't for you.

author: dawnset
review_title: Persona!
review_text: Ok, here is my review on Persona 4. In this game, they took out the most controversial thing in Persona 3: the guns and replaced them with cards. Now onto the review. Story: 10/10 The story here is simple. You play as a guy from the city who recently moved to Inaba. You then find out there has been a series of serial murders. But you are not alone, along with friends you make through your journey, you find out the truth. This may sound like a boring story, but story is not important, it is gameplay. Gameplay: 10/10 The most important part of any game. Once you survive the slow beginning, you don't want to put this game down. it is that addictive. While you and your friends investigate the murders, you have to rescue people who gets thrown in a alternate world located inside a tv. There are also social links from P3 to power up your persona. The best part of this game that they fixed from the last game is direct control. Basically, you get to control your party member's actions. so this game is addictive the first time you put this game in your PS2. Graphics: 9/10 The graphics here are so last gen. you have a few anime cutscenes and the in-game graphics look nice. but the graphics here are good for a PS2 game. Sound: 10/10 The music in this game is good. Especially the boss battle and regular battle theme. The voice acting matches the characters perfectly. You will enjoy the soundtrack this game has to offer. Characters: 10/10 The characters in this game you will like. Even if they live part from each other, they have a closer bond then your party members from Persona 3. Proof of that is when you power up your party member's social links, they can help you out in battle like take a fatal blow for you. The people you meet includes a famous store manager's son, a girl who loves kung fu movies, and the daughter of the manager of a famous inn. Point is you form a close bond with them and others. Conclusion: In conclusion, this game is fun. I guarantee you will love it the first time around. Also this game is long and even if you beat the game, you will still have fun playing this. So if you have a PS2, this will be a great addition to your pile.

author: iliveforffandwo
review_title: A disappointment from the rest of the series
review_text: I'll start off by saying I was a big fan of Persona 3. I thought it was a nice change of pace from the rest of the series and had a lot of good ideas. Although Revelations Persona was the best game in the series(especially for it's time), Persona 3 still changed up the classic RPG formula and was a great dungeon crawler for the hardcore gamer. With that said Persona 4 has done little to move the series forward and instead just takes what Persona 3 did and does it over again. The first big problem I had with the game was the difficulty felt off. The beginning bosses were very hard yet I was able to defeat the regular enemies without even trying. I mean honestly the hardest bosses in the game where in the beginning then it felt like easy sailing from there on out. Though the whole game feels like a chore, the social links were cool the first time they were done but this time I found the less interesting and also less important. I mean honestly do I want to spend the time and talk to all these people when I can just breeze through the dungeon. Of course some people will do all the social links just for the sake of completing everything but unlike in Final Fantasy or Digital Devil Saga the Persona games tend to not have an ultimate boss that will be challenging enough to make you get the ultimate Personas. On top of this the combat wasn't any better then in 3 aside from controlling your other characters it all felt the same. Some of the other stuff that was suppose to be better in this game like multiple dungeons as oppose to just one big one wasn't really any better at all. The dungeons pretty much played out like they did in 3 and added little to the experience of the game. There was no real world exploration like in Persona 2 or Revelations Persona. The story also wasn't anything that good the whole mystery solving aspect of the story was confusing and absurd it was hard to find it interesting. On top of that the true ending felt completely tacked on. This game isn't bad but it's not worth investing all the time it takes to beat it. Persona 3 was better to me in just about every aspect, even controlling your characters didn't feel much better to me because it would just make battles take longer and it was easier to put them on auto. In the end this game is really boring. You will be fighting the same boring enemies over and over and you will have to watch out the social links and stories which almost feels like a chore. Your better off playing Persona 3 and if you have already played that then you will probably not have the patience to sit through this.

author: Cymery
review_title: Return of the Shadows
review_text: After playing Persona 3 FES and the vanilla Persona 3 I came to enjoy the series quite a bit. When I started looking for the other Persona games my wallet and heart broke because 1) I couldn't find the games anywhere locally and 2) it would cost well over $80 per game on Ebay. So when I heard that Persona 4 was coming out I started saving my money and bought it a few months after my birthday. The game was worth the wait. Gameplay: 10/10 It's similar to Persona 3's with the exception of it being easier to locate your persona, items, and oh yeah the best part: you can control your party members now. Unlike Persona 3 you can control all members of your party in battle so no more stupid AI mistakes of using bufu when you desperately needed healing. Outside of battle you can run, walk, fish, and have a few part time jobs. Social links are still around and just as challenging as the last time to complete. Perhaps even more difficult as there is so much more to do in this game. My only complaint with this is that the social links aren't as deep as Persona 3's. You only use one persona this time but that's totally fine as your other party members will have a persona to help along the way. Also there are side quests to do like you did in Persona 3 but this time your helping out a temple fox. No not a girl a real fox complete with tail and everything. Sound: 9/10 Persona 4's soundtrack is much more upbeat then Persona 3's. You get relaxing tune's, you get the sound of rain, and when your fighting you get a bouncy tune to listen too that I happen to like a lot. The voice acting is really good as well. There are a few voice actors I don't recognize and I'm glad to hear some new voice talents. That said veteran players and anime watchers will recognize a few of the voice actors which is an added security blanket so if you don't like the new voice actors you can at least live with the old tried and true voice actors. Graphics: 9/10 On the whole there isn't much difference between Persona 3's and 4's design. The only real difference is that Persona 4's normal graphics are sort of fuzzed over and not as sharp as Persona 3's. However I find the anime cutscenes to be a lot better, clearer and more detailed, in this game then Persona 3's which looked half done at some points and short enough to ask yourself why the developers had even bothered to put an anime cutscene in the game at all. Story: 10/10 The is in its own way as good as Persona 3's was. However the story isn't all that serious as the previous game but it does hold its own for this game. First of all your living with your uncle and young cousin, your in high school and murders start happening all of a sudden. You make friends with 2 other main characters and it goes on from there. Basically your trying to live a normal rural high school life when bad things start happening around the town. Honestly when I write about the story it doesn't sound like a lot or even good but I don't believe in spoiling anything for you so I'll leave it at that. Just be assured the story is great but lighter then Persona 3's. Overall: 9/10 Yes Persona 4 has its issues with the graphics being a little fuzzy looking at times but graphics aren't everything. The fighting is still fun, you can actually buy lots of items to bring along with you and you can control all the characters. The story works really well and is quite meaningful to the game. The persona's are a lot of fun to use and there is some strategy needed to be used when fighting bosses. Each dungeon is completely unique and can be returned to whenever you want for levels or items needed. I'd recommend the game to anyone who likes the previous Persona games or likes rpgs in general.

author: gothiclolidollz
review_title: I'll face myself
review_text: I finished P4 a few days ago and thought I might as well review it for those who are interested. This review will only briefly touch upon the main aspects of the game without spoiling anything for those who have not finished. Story - 9/10 Persona 4 begins with our silent protagonist who moves into the small country town of Inaba to stay with his relatives for a year (due to his parent's working overseas). During his stay, he becomes involved with a gruesome murder case revolving around a mysterious show called "the midnight channel". Shortly after, he obtains the ability to call upon his inner self; his persona and can fight against the mysterious entities known as shadows. Together with a few other persona users, they attempt to unravel the case surrounding the foggy town of Inaba and catch the culprit behind the case. While P4 isn't the first game to integrate the whole "murder mystery" aspect into its plot, it does a far better job than most RPG's in terms of storytelling. While the murder mystery is there to further along the plot, it is hardly the main aspect of the story. Common themes throughout P4's plot include the ability to confront and face one's inner self. Often times, many of the main characters must come to accept a "darker" side of themselves ranging from their selfish desires to their hidden sexuality. These psychological motives and themes are what furthers along the plot rather than the central mystery itself. Gameplay - 9.5/10 Persona 4 borrows many elements from Persona 3 into its gameplay, however it never seems to feel repetitive or boring despite the similarities. For those who have played P3, you can still expect the unique combination of dungeon crawling and dating sim material interwoven. P4 improves over P3 in a number of ways by having social links directly affect character’s performance in battle. For example, by leveling up your teammate’s social links, he or she can protect you from fatal attacks which would otherwise cause you a game over. The dungeon crawling from P3 is back, but this time it is improved upon. No longer is there a huge 200+ floor dungeon but rather a handful of 8-10 floor dungeons. While the design of Tartarus from P3 got a bit repetitive towards the end, the dungeons in P4 are unique and cleverly designed to reflect the subconscious thoughts of the victims imprisoned within the dungeon. From a mundane princess’ castle to a flashy strip club, P4 has some of the most innovative dungeon designs to date which keeps the game from feeling repetitive like P3. The battle system from P3 also returns with the tried and true “1 more” system. Basically if you exploit an enemies’ weakness or score a critical hit, you are awarded with an additional turn. All-out attacks return in this installment when your party has successfully knocked down all foes. Aside from that, you now have full control over all of your party members. This not only makes it easier to form a strategy, but it also takes away the frustration from your teammates sometimes poor AI. Sound – 9/10 Before P3, nobody would ever have guessed that rap and Jpop would go together. P4 manages to do the same thing by integrating a number of Jpop themed tunes such as the main battle theme. For those who enjoy Jpop or a retro style of music reminiscent of games from the 90’s, Persona 4 will not disappoint. The voice acting is above average for almost the entire cast. Many of the actors were really able to get into character and convey their feelings, adding to the experience. I understand that in the past most dubs are pretty cheesy or terrible, but Persona 4 manages retain the same quality as Persona 3 did with its voice actors. Overall – 9.5/10 Overall, if there was one reason to still use your PS2, this is it. Not only is this my pick for PS2 game of the year, but it should also be RPG of the year. With a number of vast improvements over Persona 3, an intriguing psychological based story and a handful of extra Personas, this game should not be missed by any SMT or RPG fan. meh, 9.5 rounds up to 10 anyways. Might as well give it 10/10

author: BaalDevilKing
review_title: "At the end of the path you chose lies the truth...Believe in it and continue without faltering! "
review_text: Story: 9/10 The story is that you are a new arrival in a fictional town in Japan called "Inaba". You are living with your Uncle for a year because your parents are working overseas. After the first few days a dead body of a recently famous news reporter turns up dead. The dead body can not be identified as to the cause of death or any traces of the person who did it. A few says later another person is killed. The case begins to become deadly serious. One day you learn about a rumor of a program called the MIdnight Channel. Upon watching the Midnight Channel, you stick your hand into the TV to discover you are able to cross into another world inside the TV. Using this power you and your friend, Yosuke, go into the world of the TV and discover a bear-like creature named "Teddie". Upon meeting Teddie he takes you to another section of the TV World where you are attacked by creatures called "Shadows". Upon being attacked by the Shadows you discover a creature born from your inner thoughts called a "Persona". Using the power to cross over into the TV World and your Persona you must discover the truth behind the case and help those that are put into the TV world before the year ends. The story starts of pretty slow. You don't get full control of the MC until about 3 Hours in. But damn! Is it an experience afterwards! Unexpected Plot Twists, Solving the case, and great characters! While the story isn't anything particularly special, I'm a fan of the cliche' . Really the only way I could fault the story is how slow it started. Gameplay: 9/10 Well for starters the things they improved on. You now have full control of your team, compared to Persona 3. That's a big plus. Now when you hit one enemy with their weakness you get an extra turn even if you hit just one. You have one weapon now. THis is good because it was annoying managing the other weapons you would never use. About 70% of the roster of the Roster is the Persona from the last game. And the rest is well, new Persona. Sound: 10/10 Let's begin with the voices. Not only are the voices fantastic, but they destroy the Original Japanese voices. Johnny Yong Bosch as the main character, Yuri Lowenthal as Yosuke Hanamura, Danielle Judovits as Chie Satonaka, Amanda Winn Lee as Yukiko Amagi, Troy Baker as Kanji Tatsumi, Laura Bailey as Rise Kujikawa, Dave Wittenburg as Teddie, and Jessica Strauss as Naoto Shirogane make up the team and are fantastic! Music to my ears at how original the voice work is! David Lodge voices Ryotaro Dojima, Carrie Savage as Nanako Dojima, and Johnny Yong Bosch as Tohru Adachi. All of these are fantastic! Fitting voices that even surpass the original! Now for the music. The music this time is given a more retro feel. Which to me is a major improvement. J-Pop and Rock cover up most of the songlist. All of the songs are sung in English. Notice how I said "English" and not "Engrish". There's also tracks that fit the situation of the story. You get the drill, Creepy Moments = Creepy Moments, Awesome Moments = Awesome Music, Etcetera, Etcetera. Graphics: 8/10 The game is very pretty. Replayability: 8.5/10 Once you beat the game you'll find there is some incentive to keep you going. Maxing out other social links. Maxing the Persona Compendium. Doing certain quests. Yadda, Yadda. Overall Score: 9/10

author: Ceirrine
review_title: A PS2 game that competes with next-gen console games. Nice.
review_text: Now, we got these games with "WOW!" graphics. But does graphics determine the greatness of a game? Oh, I think not. I'm not new to RPGs. I've been playing them back around when I was in the second grade, but heck. By the time I got my hands on Persona 4, my love for RPGs got up to a new level. Okay, let's get into business. Story Well, the Persona series have our favorite "Silent" protagonists. This one is no exception. Main Character-kun has to move to Inaba because his parents are working overseas, his mother asked her brother to take care of him for a year. Later on, there is a rumor about the "Midnight Channel", it's about seeing your soulmate if you watch it in the middle of the night, plus, if it is raining. Soon after, a mysterious case popped up. Somehow, the case is related to the Midnight Channel. As the story goes on, he got a bizarre power called a "Persona", A person's inner self. From then on, Main Character-kun along with other "Persona" users decided to solve the case themselves. The whole thing about confronting oneself and accepting what you are isn't particularly new to the world of RPG. Even the part of getting a new power because of realizing who you really are is quite old, but, the way the story is progressing is rather unique. Although sometimes, a bit predictable. Rating: 9/10 Gameplay I'm sure a lot of people who played Persona 3 who looked forward to this game, notice huge improvements about the gameplay. Who wouldn't notice it? In battles, there's this follow-up attack, helping out allies if down, and other stuff. I'm pretty sure many didn't like the trial and error thing about discovering the enemy's strengths and weaknesses. Oh, there's this direct commands too, you get to control your teammates because the AI isn't very good at times. Glad that they put that in too. The social link system is still there. Eh, the social links ranks from boring to totally awesome. And for a girl social link, it's nice to have an option about remaining friends or whatnot. The gameplay had its ups and down, nevertheless, it is still awesome. Rating: 9/10 Sound This is probably one of the strengths of the game. It attracts people to listen to it from time to time. To be honest, I pause a lot of times to listen to it. Yes. As for the voice acting, I've played both Japanese and English versions of the game. I must say, this game has a lot of famous of voice actors/actresses. Ah, but if comparing the voice acting quality, I have to vote for the Japanese VAs. I'm not saying that the English VAs didn't do a good job on the voices, they DID. It's just that the Japanese voice actors/actresses had more impact on me. Rating: 10/10 Graphics It's amazing for a PS2 game, I must say. The only thing I complain about it is, when the camera moves, it is somewhat...blurring. Whatever that is called, I get a headache about it. I know someone that complains about it too, we both got sensitive eyes. The way the characters are modeled are also great. It's also nice that the characters move smoothly. Not like robots. Rating: 8.5/10 OVERALL: 9/10 A totally awesome game. If you ever see a copy of this game, go and grab it. It might not have pawnsome graphics such as next-gen games, but it's having fun that really matters.

author: Playtapus
review_title: REAL friends?! **** that! I got my PERSONA friends!
review_text: When games now-a-days cost a fortune and are not half as great as you expect them to be, one would tend to be skeptical towards buying a new one. At least that's the problem with me. Not even Billy Mays and his brilliant advertising skills could convince me of buying a game unless it's on the bargain bin. But Persona 4...this game...I just had a feeling it would be good. I was wrong, this game is not good. This game is AMAZING! It is worth every penny and more! This could very well be the last RPG for the PS2 and a testament of why this is the best console on the market. I don't wanna write any more useless crap so I'll get to the nitty-gritty. Story: 9\10 The basic outline of the story is this: a rumor is going around school that by looking at a TV screen at 12:00 AM on a rainy nights, the face of your soulmate will be revealed. Meanwhile a series of bizarre murders begins where the cause of death is unknown but is somehow connected to this "Midnight Channel". As the murders continue, the protagonist and his companions discover a door to another world in search for the culprit. The key to this door is the power within their souls; their other selves--their Personas...I took that directly from the booklet because I couldn't have put it better myself. Sounds interesting right? It is, but what really makes this game's story stand out is the character development. The idea of facing your true self is a recurring concept within the game and boy let me tell you it is very well done. I can't really delve into it without spoiling it but let me just say that each character adds a HUGE amount of depth into this game. Graphics: 9\10 To me, graphics are not really a big factor to me when it comes to video games. Although I gotta say those bastards at Square-Enix have spoiled me. This game has very nice graphics, very nice. The cut-scenes are animated, that might turn some people off but it really fits the game. Gameplay: 9/10 This a turn-based RPG mixed with...I dunno what's it called, life simulator? The game takes place one day at a time, you're high school student and somehow you gotta manage to balance your daily activities while trying to solve the murder mystery by defeating "shadows". Sounds...not so epic, but believe me it is much more than that. The flow of the game is like this: Go to school at day, choose to hang out with friends or solve the latest mystery in the afternoon and then at night do part-time work or study. You might be asking yourself, "What's so important about hanging out with friends, working and studying?" Well by doing so you can establish what's called a Social Link. You need this in order to obtain better Personas and become stronger. Other than armor and weapons, you need Personas for various abilities and stat growth. Think of Personas as Pokemon based on different religions. That sounds almost better, no? Well it is, dang it! Sound: 10\10 The best thing in the game. The music is catchy and fitting with every escenario. The voice acting is top-notch. Some people complain because it doesn't have the original japanese voice-over, that's their problem. I happen to think the voices are great and if you don't like it, you can always mute it. Conclusion: 9\10 Mr. T says: "I pity the foo' who don't buy this game!"

author: FalseGodsSlayer
review_title: "I AM THOU AND THOU ART I"
review_text: “I AM THOU, AND THOU ART I” “Embrace yourself”, means to accept oneself as he or she is genuinely be, and not pretending to be an individual that totally different from oneself. What one fear the most lies within oneself and hidden deep within one’s personality as “shadows”; Sometimes it is difficult to admit what one truly is, but that doesn’t mean one can just deny the existence of that part within him or her, because like it or not, that part is still oneself. These messages are strongly implied in the recently released Playstation 2 game, Persona 4. This highly anticipated game, developed by Atlus, starts with the main character, that just recently transferred to a little suburban town of Inaba, stumbled into serial bizzare murder cases, and unnatural urban legend, known as “The Midnight Channel”, that happened in that peaceful town. Curiosity rises, and through the newfound strength, the main character set on the journey to reveal the truth behind all of the murders and things that lie beyond the “other” world. As one of the character of this game, Igor, said that “Persona” is merely a facade, another face that one used to connect to other people and beings; But the truth is that through those social connections, one can truly expand his or her hidden potentials to the maximum. So does this game, which strongly emphasized in the main character’s social relations rather than strengthening through force. With the complex and intense story, gamers are obliged to keep the main character in shape, both in the field of academic, social lives, and strength. With an incredible gameplay and captivating, yet touching social links’ stories, one could find it difficult to part with this game, even if one managed to finish the whole game. Apart from that, with new A.I. and battle system, as well as the new breed of enemies and bosses, this game could be challenging to any veteran gamers and Shin Megaten fans. And also, supported by great music, composed by the legendary Shoji Meguro, it is not exaggerated to say that this game is the one of the best games in the year of 2008. In the conclusion, with near-perfection gameplay and mechanics, complex and touching story, this game is worthy to be given a place for one the best game ever. Sometimes, people could forgot who they truly are because they fear to admit one side of themselves that they keep hidden. But, this game, it reminded us to be what we are, to “embrace” ourselves as what we are. Was there any video games that gave great morals, like this game? Igor, one of the character in this game, once said that the main character’s power was similiar to the number zero; It was empty, but held the infinite possibilities. Same goes to this amazing game, it’s just an ordinary role playing game like other RPGs as well, but it gives a great impact to people hearts and feelings. Doubtful, try it! It Does impact your lives.

author: Baalji_Baalstar
review_title: Well, you all saw it coming eventually.
review_text: Criticizing the World with Baal: Persona 4 My history with the MegaTen series has been a decent one. I started by playing Digital Devil Saga 2 then moved onto P3, Devil Summoner, Nocturne, Digital Devil Saga 1 and finally this game. And my opinions? In respective order: Fantastic, Meh, Great, Great, Fantastic and I'm making this review for a reason! There's more after that but we're only mentioning what I played first before this. Persona 4 is a special kind of game... okay, not really but we're speaking hypothetically here. If Digital Devil Saga is the King of the Megaten Castle, then the Persona series are the four obnoxious cousins of the Prince and Princess (Devil Summoner and Devil Survivor) the children their mothers (The Main Megaten Series) equally obnoxious sister (If...). The first one is a bit annoying but good at heart, the second one is a jerk with a heart of gold, the third one mopes around for about a month before somehting annoys them enough to do something interesting and the fourth one has a short-attention span. But enough of my rambling, let's get to the review in this review. In Persona 4 you play as the Protagonist (duh), who is forced to go live with his Uncle and Cousin for a year because they're too busy with their jobs and neglecting him. When you make it to the rural town of Inaba, strange things begin happening that circulate around the murder of a famous TV reporter. You then meet up with a bunch of... "interesting" characters who pretty much force you to help them investigate these murders and find the culprit, because there's nothing better for 16-Year Old's in Japan to do, I guess. Oh and one of them has a personal grudge against the murderer, but it's not really his place to get mad about something that had nothing to do with him about a person who didn't even like him, so you'll stop caring about him soon enough. In the process of all of this, you gain the ability to summon a Persona, a physical manifestation of your mind you can use to fight Shadows for you. They can be fused, summoned and even have some surreal designs. What are shadows you ask? Well, you're probably not asking that but humor me. Shadows are creatures that are in the World of the TV that you have to fight before they kill someone who is thrown in the TV. Oh you didn't know there was a TV World or people being thrown into the TV? WELL YOU PROBABLY SHOULD'VE ASKED. Yes, over the process of the game people will be thrown into TVs and you have to save them from being killed by the Shadows otherwise it is redo time and they spearhead you as the leader of all of this... enjoy that title, because it's not as much of a free title as it entails. Now let's get to the game part of the video game. The gameplay of actual battles is Turn-Based, you choose your moves, hit an opponent with them and wail on them with attack, magic and skills until they die. It's a very well-constructed battle system that makes the game somewhat fun to play, but if you feel you're having too much fun and are tired of your teammates following exactly what you say (Like they're supposed to do since you're supposed to be the leader) then you can turn on the AI and they can make they're own stupid decisions that will get them killed in the end, just like they do in the story. The dungeon crawling leaves something to be desired, maybe it's the fact that the dungeons are randomized and this makes navigating them later an enormous pain in the backside. That and all of the dungeons are either have bland designs, easily beatable bosses or dumb interruptions at every given turn. Then there's Arcana Chances, which after most fights will happen. The arcana chances are made of every Tarot Card (Except The World) in the Major Arcana making for a total of 21 cards and 41 possible results seeing as how they can also end up upwards or downwards (Excluding The Fool). The cards have varying effects ranging from upgrading abilities to sapping all of your SP to 1. Now, I'm going to need a paragraph for this because I've got a lot to talk about here, maybe two. The worst part of this game comes up now, the S. Link/Calendar System. The S. Link system allows you to converse with people and go through their stories while getting more EXP for your Persona you fuse to get them better abilities faster and get you some interesting stories. The stat system for S. Links and Jobs is made up of five different stats that level up as you do more activities such as reading books and asking the teacher if he called you a loser. The Calendar system puts things on a date, certain weather will happens on certain dates affecting who you can do S. Links with, what new shadows you can fight in the TV World to get better weapons/armor/accessories and even progress the story. It splits each day into a few sections (Morning, Lunch, Afternoon, After School and Night) Sounds fun and intuitive, right? WRONG. The S. Link system makes the game much more tedious to play since you are limited by what you can do per day (Since only two of the parts of the day are commonly playable), the S. Links take more time to complete than they really should (Not as much as in Persona 3, but still annoying) as they overstay their welcome after a while, the jobs you get don't pay enough for you to actually do much with since money is pretty annoying to collect unless you use one of the Arcana Chance cards and even that doesn't last long enough for you to actually get much with it. What's worse is some of them can only be accesse Although some of the stories are interesting, they don't provide much to the actual game other adding more EXP to your fused Persona, so they seem entirely pointless as they could've easily been replaced with something else and it would've been even more efficient. The Calendar System is a test in patience as you will have to make a schedule thanks to it. While making a schedule doesn't sound bad, I don't play video games to make a schedule, I play them to be entertained, a schedule is not entertaining. It gets even more annoying when you realize that pretty much anything you do takes up part of a day, yes, even eating and entering the TV take up part of a day and since you can't enter the TV at night, you're most likely going to be giving up a few days that could've been better spent doing something more important, like insulting the Twilight Franchise or Eating Stuff out of your Fridge. But at least you get a free month later in the game to make-up for some stuff but all of this is at the cost of the game's pacing. The music is hit-and-miss. There are times when the tracks in the soundtrack are fantastic and then there are other times when it's just abhorrent. For example, the game starts out on a nice piano orchestra, then you get to the beginning when you name your character and there's another nice piano orchestral, then you get to Inaba and there's a nice instrumental piece, then when you get out of school later when you have control of the character, what of all things begins playing? Crappy J-Pop music sung by a Japanese woman who can't sing quite well and very annoying instrumentals. The music in battles are fantastic for the most part, the actually dungeon crawling tracks are hit-and-miss as well. The voice-acting of the game is really good for the most part. Several voice-actors did well on their parts but some were just downright obnoxious compared to the very good ones. Then there's two voices that just change quality. Outside of battle one voice changes from perfect to downright bad, while the other is quite good outside of battle but in actual combat it's quite an annoying voice with some pretty badly delivered lines. Although this game does have one of the best performances from Johnny Yong Bosch I've ever seen, so we'll give it a pass on voice-acting and move on to (What I hope) is the last part of this review, the characters. The characters in this game are... well, eccentric. Not that that's bad, it's just that... it's nothing special, they're all just a bunch of random character archetypes. You have The Obnoxious Leader, Tomboy, Well-mannered girl with problems because there is no other kind of Well-mannered girl, the stupid muscled delinquent because once again there is no other kind of delinquent, the annoying mascot character, the annoying flirty girl, and the too young to be in this profession but still does so because they're trying to do good for people and a whole bunch more. Although some are actually well-built upon these cliche's to be forgiven of this. In summary (and for those who didn't bother to read the entire thing and just wanted the cliffnotes) Persona 4 is an average game. It has a decent story but below-average pacing, hit-or miss music but good voice-acting, fun combat system but annoying dungeon system and to top it all off, an annoying gameplay gimmick that could've taken some fine-tuning before putting this in an actual game. But then again this is all just my opinion and I know that those of you who disagree with me will respect my opinion enough to not bug me about it. ...Snrk.

author: Zeik999
review_title: Persona 4 another hit for the series
review_text: Persona 4 is the indirect sequel to Persona 3. Their stories are unrelated but they share many Gameplay elements such as personas and social links. This game has followed a very successful series of games with persona 3 getting the most hype. setting that aside this game was really good so if you lie Persona its worth checking out. Story The story for persona 4 is very mysterious and kinda creepy. It starts out with your character moving to Inaba to live with your uncle and cousin. You move there because your parents are working overseas. I know it isn't the most unique setup but shortly after arriving a strange murder occurs. On top of that there is a strange rumor that on a rainy night if you stand in front of your TV at midnight you'll see your soul mate. The whole story is a mystery that involves both this rumor and murders that start happening. you find out that the people are being sucked into the TV and you and your friends are the only one who can save them. This story is pretty cool but not completely unique there are a few other games that involve being sucked into a TV. Gameplay The game is divided into two areas the TV world and the real world. In the TV world you try to save the people trapped there while fighting monsters called shadows. To fight these monsters your characters must utilize a special power called Persona. Personas are the true form of a person's personality and each character has their own persona with its own strengths and weaknesses. The main character is the only person capable of having more than one persona. The TV world is pretty much the main RPG part. You run around and fight monsters level up collect items that sort of thing. In the real world you play through the main character's life. you get to go to school, get called on by the teachers, join club and so on. the cool part is the social links. The social links are just like they sound, they are the connections you have with other people. they give extra strength to your persona when you create them through fusion. Also the way you interact with the characters can alter the story somewhat but nothing major. Graphics and sound Persona's graphics are okay they aren't phenomenal nor are they bad. The game features plenty of anime style cutscenes and when you talk to important characters an anime style image of the character shows up mostly to help you understand their mood. The music feature in the game is some kind of Japanese pop. This game is definitely worth checking out at least once. This game is addicting and fun but after a while gets repetitive so if that's not really your thing then this game might not be for you.

author: AnalyticalGamer
review_title: ...Wow, Atlus, can you do any wrong?
review_text: Story: Let’s start with one of best aspects of Persona 4. The story is absolutely phenomenal. Persona 4 boasts an extremely complex and developed plot, and it carries plenty of emotional impact. Through the genius Social Link system, you meet an array of different characters – each unique in their own way. The development of these characters is absolutely flawless. The story carries no plot holes, and is executed perfectly. The only problem is that the game ends too soon; cutting short the last 3 months of the magnificent story. – 9.8/10 Gameplay: Persona 4 boasts some really fun and frighteningly difficult gameplay. Throughout the game, you’ll be struggling to make it by each boss. Difficulty doesn’t equal bad; though, as Persona 4’s gameplay is extremely addicting. There are literally hundreds of skills and strategies you can use to wipe the floor of enemies; the same applies to the enemies as well, as they’ll destroy you with the very same skills. Overall, you’ll have a wonderful time and a heart attack at the same time while playing the game. – 9.4/10 Sound: Persona 4 boasts a great soundtrack. The soundtrack isn’t exemplary, but it’s definitely catchy. There are many memorable tracks, but a few get a bit repetitive and annoying. The soundtrack is diverse and overall pleasant to listen to. The voice acting is stellar, easily some of the best on the PS2. – 8.6/10 Graphics: The graphics for Persona 4 are solid. They’re not Final Fantasy quality or anything, but they’re good and they work. The AMVs that play are of mediocre quality, the animation for them is a bit choppy, but they look alright. Persona 4 isn’t a graphical masterpiece, but it's not a big deal. – 7.7/10 Controls: I honestly don’t believe there’s anything to say here other than the controls work great and are completely flawless. – 10/10 Replay Value: The replay value of this game is absolutely monstrous. There are nearly 200 personas to collect, tons of social links to master, a superboss, bonus bosses, customization of persona skills… and so much more. You can spend hundreds of hours with Persona 4. – 10/10 Overall: Persona 4 is a prime example of what an RPG should be. Persona 4 is fun, challenging, has a great story, a nice soundtrack, good graphics, and TONS of replay value. It’s an example of a dying breed in today’s RPG market, and shows that an RPG doesn’t need flashy graphics to be outstanding. I can only hope that more RPGs strive to be like Persona 4. 9.5/10

author: coltonmray94
review_title: One of the most unique and ambitious games of the last decade
review_text: After beating Persona 3: FES earlier in the year, I immediately acquired a copy of its sequel, a game I'd heard about for years but never experienced. After putting in 80 hours over the past two months, I can say this game is definitely an experience - an emotional roller coaster. At the start of the game, I wasn't sure if I was going to like it as much as P3 , but by the end, I was in love. More than any game I can think of, I became so attached to these characters. Over the year of time you spend with Yosuke, Chie, Yukiko, and the others, you learn so much about their personalities, fears, and dreams that you can't help but care about them, and you'll be thinking about them long after the game ends. The cast is excellent. You learn the streets of Inaba, and though it is a little more cramped than the island from P3 , its still cozy. The story is a little more grounded than P3 , at first seeming like a Scooby Doo murder mystery, but it eventually blossoms into much more. You and your band of friends roam the streets and dungeons searching for clues as to who is murdering the residents of your town and what is behind the mysterious Midnight Channel and TV world that you have access to. The story is not as relentlessy dark and depressing as P3 , but there are still some very serious elements. Persona 4 addresses all kinds of issues, from struggles with gender and sexuality, the influence of mass media, repressed emotions, sociopathic teens, etc. In order to master their personas, each member of the gang must confront their shadows, the worst parts of themselves that they are most afraid of: repressed sexuality, jealousy, fear, rage, immaturity. It is only by accepting these parts of themselves that they can truly change and become heroes. The graphics are wonderful and expressive. The music is somehow even better than its predecessor. Voice acting is top-notch. The dungeons are more varied. The events are fun and hilarious. Bosses are tough, but rarely frustratingly hard. Altogether, this is not only one of the best games I've played this year, it is one of the best games I've played in my life. I highly recommend this series to all RPG fans and anyone who enjoys a good story and wonderful characters. You will not be disappointed.

author: fireemblemomega
review_title: I present to you the game of the year, possibly of all time
review_text: I have played a bevy of JRPGs since the Sega Genesis era to now. Phantasy Star, Suikoden, Wild Arms, Final Fantasy even, I have played quite a number of games that defined and molded the genre. Until Persona Q, I had only tried number 3 once, and didn't get far as my impatient nature conceded that I wasn't quite in the know of what to do. Persona 5 has changed this. The game was in development for so long that most doubted it would come out. It was in that, "So it's like how long KH fans are waiting for number 3?" moment. However it is definitely safe to say that it was worth the wait. Expect this review to be heavily biased, as it's evoked the very nature of my soul to sing wildly, an unexpected resonance that never would've occurred without this game. Story: You take control of yet another silent protagonist that you can name however you like. While there isn't an option to choose gender, that's unimportant in the long scheme of things, as the story revolves around this young man and the fate he's been forced into enduring. At the beginning of the game, you see him intervening with a drunken man trying to force a woman into a car, and the drunk man falls and is hurt. He shouts how he will sue, and the scene fades away. Apparently he won, as you're now in the care of one Sojiro Sakura, a grumpy cafe owner who has, for some reason, agreed to take you in, despite your now criminal record. While you're on probation, any reason you step out of bounds will result you being in juvenile hall, as well as essentially kissing your future goodbye. Oh yeah, and the game shows you the ropes in a tutorial that essentially shows that you're in the present, and once things go awry, you're going to be reliving these events as you explain what happened and why you do what you do. More on that later. It goes from there that you're introduced to your new school and, no surprise, no one likes you immediately, as it was somehow leaked that you're a criminal and, for whatever reason, the principal was ok with your coming to his school, a rarity for the school system in Japan. It's at this time that you visit the cognitive world for the first time with Ryuji, an atypical, typical right-hand man. You learn how you can change things from distorted desires from Morgana, a prisoner there, and it becomes a desperate struggle to keep the tentative peace you just acquired here. This brings the synopsis to a close as any more would spoil it. I can say, though, that the story was a masterpiece in craft, bringing a sense of finding ones place in the world, along with how one individual can influence an entire story. In fact, I'd be hard-pressed to find a single good comparison to the MC here, as he's the Swiss Army Knife of the game. When your purpose is made clear, it becomes an exercise in how well you balance your game life, if you will, with your real life. Exams still occur, relationships can be made and increased, and even social aspects must be tended to. It's quite a bit to take in at once! However, the game isn't shy about giving you a generous amount of time to cultivate these pieces of your life, allowing your dungeon crawling to be important, but not so overwhelming that you can't draw power from your allies into the different Personas you can use. Boy do they add to the analogy I made earlier. The Fool, depicted by a zero, has infinite possibilities. While your teammates will be stuck with one, and only one, Persona the entire game, you can swap out as needed, making the MC one of the most powerful characters in the game, if not the most. Adaptability will be key to taking down some of the more powerful enemies, and you'll quickly be talking and fusing your Personas up as time goes on. While this may sound like a pain, the game is quick to point out different ways to really see how you can recruit easier and even summon ones you've snagged before from the sea of thought. This is crucial, as some Personas may prove to be the only reason you'll make it through some boss fights. The story itself is a tear jerker, as you're telling the story in the past, reliving the events that brought to your initial capture, telling of your various triumphs, of the villains you took down, and how you're not a killer, just someone making a difference. Each time you make a bond, you revisit this scenario, as if you're needing a reminder that you're in the police's custody. I didn't say care because you'll see for yourself that their hospitality is lacking, and once again, you're being treated like the Devil himself. As you explain yourself, you'll find that events are rushing up to meet the present in one of the biggest blindsides anyone could cook up, and it's delightful. The story alone makes the game worth it. However, there are other aspects to appreciate. Graphics: The comic style of Persona is back, as you'll notice that quite fast. The colors, the lines, they jump out and capture your attention, arresting your psyche to pay attention to every mundane detail. The dungeons themselves are twisted worlds that carry weight, bringing a selection of variety that you may not have expected, certainly I didn't. While it can get a bit dull seeing certain places over and over, these didn't do that to me, keeping my sense of wonder and, in some cases, bringing out my inner Indiana Jones. In battle, the graphics do, at times, feel extremely repetitive, but that's to be expected as you'll be fighting a lot. Each enemy looks alive, ready to use their vim and vigor to wreck your face, but at the same time, fearing what you can do to them in turn. It's nothing short of glorious as you just simply enjoy the view at times. While you can argue that some places look like any place you'd find in a game, I could argue that this doesn't detract, rather, it helps your suspension of disbelief to continue enjoying this masterpiece. Sounds: If this game had VR capability, I highly believe that you would find true immersion. Not only do the voices come across as crisp, completely level and wonderful to listen to, each person has a unique personality that really captures what they're all about. Attacks clash, and it sounds like it really hurts when you land a nasty blow or take one yourself. Music doesn't bore either, bringing an OST that truly rivals most any soundtrack of any time. Replayability: Fair. There is a new game plus mode, in which you keep certain pieces and can continue to develop others. It's more an exercise in, what did you miss? Did you get the ending you wanted? Did you find every secret, do everything, fuse every Persona? It's easy to get lost in this, finding purpose again, but I admit, that I find it hard to play any JRPG again because of how awesome this was, which brings me to the final point. Verdict: Game of the year, perhaps of all time. 10/10, get this, play it, you will never be disappointed. If your soul resonates with this, if you find yourself feeling it, if your tears flow freely at times and the feeling of triumph fills your very spirit, then this is your game. I recommend this to everyone, even people who don't have time to play JRPGs anymore. Not only did Atlus raise the bar, I have a hard time seeing anyone beating it anymore. There's no doubt that whatever games do next, this will stand as a testament to being one of the best of all time, and is now my personal favorite, beating many other great games to become the champion.

author: Emi3280
review_title: As a newcomer to the series, I'm more than satisfied
review_text: I’d like to first talk about the backstory of how I got to buy this game, considering that I’ve never played another Shin Megami Tensei or Persona game beforehand. I had just finished the last game I bought, so it crossed my mind to check the list of games released this year. The most recent title was Persona 5. At first it didn’t catch my attention, but after realizing it’s the fifth entry of its series, I realized it should be good considering many game series don’t get that far. That’s the moment when I decided to check if they had it in stock in my nearest local retailer, and there it was. That same day I picked up my copy, and now here I am, about a week and a half later. Finished the game about an hour ago, and the only thing in my mind was to write a review about it. The last JRPG I enjoyed this much was Chrono Trigger, and I’m not exaggerating in the comparison. Let’s start with the review. Story The story is what you would expect from a Japanese writer. It all starts off with the protagonist, who apparently protected a woman from an abusing man, which got injured and sued, resulting in the main character being put on probation and sent off to another city in the country. After this, the game shows a sequence of the MC escaping from a casino, but ultimately fails and gets caught. He then gets sent to interrogation, where a prosecutor tells him to explain everything that happened from the very first moment. The game then goes back several months in the calendar, giving the illusion that everything that’ll happen is a flashback, or the protagonist simply recalling everything that has happened. After this it’s impossible to explain without spoiling anything, but it’s safe to say that you’ll feel confused at times, asking yourself questions like what’s really going on. Those questions are what fuel the story, you always want to know more. While it does drag on at times, the storytelling really keeps you on your toes most of the time while trying to keep it simple. I wouldn’t expect less from a product coming from Japan, after all they’re the best in creating enjoyable fantasy stories like this one. Story: 10/10 Gameplay This is where Persona 5 shines above the competition. There are so many aspects to it that you can’t simply describe it all together even if you tried. First of all the game is a JRPG, so you can expect classic turn based combat, something that never grows old if the creators know how to keep it fresh. You have the basic commands that you could suppose would be in a turn based battle system, regular attack, special attacks called ‘Persona’, which are kind of souls that each have unique techniques and weaknesses for confronting the enemy, which I will describe later on the review. You also have your gun, which is another type of attack, and block. The other functions are changing your party members and analyzing your opponent’s weaknesses, but those don’t need a full mention. Like I was stating before, each character has a Persona, with the exception of the protagonist, who has the ability to harness any Persona you can encounter. Each Persona has a unique set of weaknesses and techniques that they can learn, which at first can look like the standard “fire is super effective against water” system that was made popular by Pokemon, but Atlus had a slight different approach. Each Persona doesn’t have a specific ‘type’, but instead they all have a different set of weaknesses and attacks that they’ll learn as you level them up. Also the types are not the typical elements that you’d see in a regular RPG (water, ground, etc). While some common types are in the system like Electric, Fire, and Psychic, there are some others that newcomers to the series like myself wouldn’t know what’s super effective against them, or what they’re good for, for example Nuclear, Curse, Almighty, the list goes on. The learning curve can be confusing at first, but once you get the hang of it you’ll really enjoy this unique battle system. Moving on, the battle system is not all there is to Persona 5. Another aspect to the game is that it’s a dungeon crawler. You explore dungeons, or in this case Palaces, resolving puzzles to proceed further on while confronting monsters, which in this game are called Shadows. Most of the puzzles don’t require much thinking, but later on the game you’ll have to really use your brain for resolving some of the harder ones, after all that’s what we’re all looking for, a challenge. Yet another aspect to take into account about the game is the world outside the dungeons. In the real world, you’re a normal student, living a normal scholar life. You have stats to work on, which can have an impact in your interactions with the other NPCs, which the game refers to as Confidants. These stats are Charm, Knowledge, Guts, Proficiency, and Kindness. As you advance in your relationship with your Confidants, you’ll eventually need to also level up your social stats, which is good because it gives you something to do other than the dungeon crawling. Advancing in the ranks with your Confidants not only gives you benefits in battle, but it also provides us side stories from each character, most of them interesting, adding more value to the story aspect of the game. Something I’d like to mention is that the game is packed with dialogue. Most of the time you’ll have to choose from multiple options, which at the end have almost the same outcome, just a slight different line as an answer proceeding your choice. All of this sums up to thinking that the game has a strong resemblance with a visual novel, which shouldn’t be surprising taking into account that it’s a story-driven game. All these aspects fit together like pieces of a puzzle, and the end result is Persona 5. The gameplay couldn’t be any better for a JRPG. Gameplay: 10/10 Graphics I’d like to mention that I don’t think that what makes a game are the graphics. Sure, it’s nice to have high-end, extremely polished to the point that you can see the sweat running down the forehead of the characters (yes I’m exaggerating), but at the end of the day, what really makes a game good is how it plays out. While Persona 5 doesn’t have exceedingly polished graphics, it perfectly illustrates what a good JRPG looks like. The character models are well detailed, the Personas are top notch, the lightning effect in the textures really worked out. Tokyo is really lively, while the NPCs look rather bland, the areas are really well detailed for not being specifically an open world game. The anime cutscenes are spectacular, I really liked every time one of those popped up. Overall, the developers did a really nice job with how they managed the graphics. Graphics: 9/10 Sound/Music I wasn’t expecting the music in the game. Considering that the last JRPG that I played was Chrono Trigger, my expectations of the OST were pretty high considering that game had a masterpiece soundtrack. The game primarily uses Acid Jazz, a genre I hadn’t listen up until I played this game. At first it felt weird, considering I wasn’t expecting it at all, but while progressing in the game I grew quite fond of the soundtrack used. Sometimes when I’m not playing the song played in the game’s evenings plays in my mind unconsciously. It’s a very unique soundtrack that fits the theme of the game perfectly. Moving on to the voice acting, the game offers you two choices, English and the original Japanese audio, which is available as free DLC in the PS Store. I personally like everything in the original language it was made, so I played the game in Japanese. There’s not much to say about it, it’s pretty much on spot everywhere. Overall, the sound of the game was pretty much flawless. Sound/Music: 10/10 Replay Value First I’d like to mention that this is a very long game, with special emphasis in the ‘very’. It’s extremely long. At the very end of my playthrough I had clocked in 79 hours, and I was rushing at times since I really wanted to know what was going to happen next in the story. There is so much to it that you can’t do everything in a single playthrough, if you really want to 100% the game you’ll have to make multiple runs. The game offers a New Game+ for this. Instead of starting all over in every save, you get to keep certain progress for your next run, like the Persona compendium, which is basically the bestiary from other RPGs. Since it’s a linear story-driven game, you’ll basically know what’s going to happen, which kind of kills off the feeling of not knowing what’s going on, but if you don’t mind that then it’s a really good game for going back to every once in a while once you accomplish everything there is in it. Replay Value: 10/10 Buy or Pass? This game is most definitely a buy. I’m really fortunate that I found out about it while randomly searching for a game to buy, I can say without a doubt that this game is worth the $60 price tag. If you’re into JRPGs this is a must have. If you like what the Japanese masterminds exports to the world, this is also a must have. This is a game that I would highly recommend to anyone with a PS4 or a PS3, it’s a unique experience that if you like story-driven games you simply can’t miss out. Buy or Pass? Definitely buy! Recap: Story: 10/10 Gameplay: 10/10 Graphics: 9/10 Sound/Music: 10/10 Replay Value: 10/10 Overall Score: 9.8/10

author: PrinnyRaider
review_title: Spoiler Free JP copy Review
review_text: Disclaimer: This is a review of a physical Japanese copy for the PS4. I only have a elementary command of the Japanese language, but understood 85% of what was going on in terms of story. Since playing Persona 4 in 2007 I have been waiting for the next installment of Persona for almost a decade now. There have been a lot of fears that I had about Persona 5 considering the all of the Persona 4 spin offs of varying quality that have been made during the wait. After 90 hours of playing the Japanese Version and beating it for the first time, I believe its safe to say that Persona 5 does not suck. What you have is an experience that is a great fusion of classic Shin Megami Tensei and what we know as Persona today. Presentation When people think about Persona 5 given from what they have seen from any of the trailers for the game is that it oozes style, and that remains true throughout the game. The game's color of choice is red (where P3 was blue and P4 was yellow) and is highlighted by an assortment of black and white. For the most part it really works considering that most of the text boxes are still white text on a black background. I bring up the color choice because you see a lot of red when you play the game normally through its UI and various menus, which have really stepped it up since Persona 4. Menus are fun, dynamic, and almost always include little character art that makes it really fun to just look at. Of course when talking about stuff to look at there are the characters! Shigenori Soejima is still Atlus' go-to guy for character designer, and main guy for designing trendy teenagers for a main cast. Whenever there was a story scene in which the characters' are just standing around talking, I found myself always looking at Soejima's character portraits rather than the actual scene. If you liked the design of the characters from the previous 2 Persona games you will enjoy these characters...except for this one little hiccup that has to do with Soejima's particular style of drawing. In the past Soejima has been known for drawing really long necks, and that is still true in Persona 5. The only consolation is that its less noticeable as there are usually accessories or clothes to obscure this fact, and even then its only apparent if you really take your time too look at it. As for the 3D models its nothing to write home about. They're basically 3D mannequins that have their usual animation cycles, and not as highly detailed as the models from something like Final Fantasy XV. In my game, on top of some general stiffness there were a few occasions of hair physics freaking out and causing spasms on a character that was standing still. That is about it for complaints though. Everything else such as the major cutscenes (that were not anime) and the demons/persona in this game they really put a nice touch on them. They “bathed” the models in this neat light that give them a cool ethereal feel to them, and it looks great. The environments are also pretty varied, which is a great welcome. The non-dungeon parts really made me feel like I was in Tokyo. Although it was not the level of detail of something like GTA where everything is up to scale and the facilities were made exactly to mimic real life. In the beginning of the game I was a little worried that I wouldn't know how to go anywhere because the main mode of transportation is the train system. Luckily for me they would add fast travel menu, which actually seems to represent the real life train lines that you would find everyone using in Tokyo proper. The dungeons however are a different story as these places do not actually exist. Story dungeons have a distinct feel to them as they take different forms of fantasy, but nonetheless are always really cool to be in and look at. Lastly, there are the anime cutscenes that are usually used to present scenes in which the ingame engine probably could not produce on its own. These are usually large action scenes that require a lot of movement to get a story point across. Not much to say about it here other than the the (Japanese) voice acting does not get super quiet during these animated cutscenes like they did in Persona 4. Sound Anybody who has played Persona 3 or 4 will know that the music of Persona has a very unique and distinct sound to them. Largely in part to Shoji Meguro who is back to work on Persona 5. What seems to be the main theme of the game is the use of Acid Jazz, but of course with Meguro's spin on it. When I first started the game and I heard the song that plays with the opening animated intro I said to myself “Oh yeah this sounds like Persona.” Meguro, along with Lyn who provides vocals for any song in the game that has vocals, really did a great job. After a long day of work/school its always such a relief to hear Lyn sing in “Beneath the Mask.” Gameplay There are a lot of things to talk about when it comes to gameplay so I will begin with aspects of the game that pertains to things done outside of dungeon and then inside. First of all there's the Velvet Room. Quite the familiar place with a few extra bells and whistles. These bells and whistles are new ways to use persona and even items to reach any particular goal. The key here is experimentation and there is really no wrong answer. Stat building returns in Persona 5 and there are five stats to build: Charm, Intelligence, Courage, Diligence, and Expression/Empathy. These are my own translations on the stats, but it is more or less the same stats that were in Persona 4. These still directly affect who you can talk to and what activities you are able to do. So getting max stats is always something to strive for. Not much to say here other than go at it however you want as there are a multitude of ways to build each stat. Obviously there will be certain stats that take more priority over the others as the players will learn more and more efficient ways of doing Max co-op/social link runs. On the topic of Co-operations/Social Links, these are have a much bigger impact on gameplay than simply gaining access to stronger persona for your team. As you progress through a relationship with a particular person you will be ranked at 1 and move your way up to 10, thus completing the co-op/social link. In Persona 5, each rank may give you a perk that will directly affect gameplay in one way or another. Perks can be things such as “a fraction of experience for non active party members” or even “gain the ability to switch active party members in battle.” These perks are generally very useful and give greater incentive to do as much socializing as you possibly can. Now getting to the dungeons proper there are a lot of new and old things that present. Things that have stayed the same is the turn based combat system with the knockdown mechanic. The ways you can a knock down is through either exploiting a weakness or getting a critical hit through a physical attack of some type. In terms of weaknesses there are now 2 new forms of magic on top of the previous 6, and physical is broken up into 2 types: normal and piercing attacks. Now when a knockdown occurs you can still go for a follow up (1 more), and when all the enemies are down you can go for an All Out Attack or a negotiation. One very welcome change to the game is that if it is possible to exploit a known weakness on a character's turn you must simply hit R1 and then confirm to get an easy knockdown. The All Out Attack is still the same as previous games but negotiation is new. From negotiations you can recruit enemies to be persona, which is reminiscent of the older SMT games. Alternatively you can choose to extort money and items from them, which is useful for when you want a fight to end and you already have a particular enemy in your persona arsenal. For combat each option you have is typically tied to a button rather then having to scroll through a menu. These buttons will be block, attack with weapon, persona skill, use item, use gun (piercing attack), and so on. Note that teammates will be working on AI in the very beginning so it is typically recommended that you change that to have party members take orders from the player instead. There is also very nice quality of life addition in this game that I have not seen since SMT:Digital Devil Saga 2. At the press of a button you can heal your active party to full HP using the pool of SP from the members of the party that has access to heal skills. Onto the dungeons themselves it is very different from Persona 3 and 4. They are no longer randomly generated except for the 1 large dungeon that is known as Mementos. Every story dungeon has a set structure and have very light platforming and puzzle solving. A very welcome change to break up the monotony of randomly generated levels. What is particularly special about these dungeons is that there is waist high cover everywhere for the player to hide behind. These are used to hide from enemies that patrol the dungeons and allow you to attack them from cover to give your party the first turns in the battle. This is how most combat should initiate as enemies are pretty tough in this game. Allowing enemies to take turns can spell disaster, and in hard mode getting ambushed is almost a guaranteed game over. Though there are times where sometimes things will just not work out. This is the first time in my experience that stealth has been a mechanic, and it shows. Sometimes you will see that you want to initiate a battle by running behind an enemy, and if you fail to get that back attack they will turn around and hit you instead. There will be times where it will be unclear whether you failed a prompt or it was just the game not working as intended. The key in most of the situations is to stay healed up and alert! Story Probably one of the most important aspects for many people when it comes to Persona; the story here is decent for what it is. First of all lets address the themes and motifs from the previous games. Persona 3 was Sorrow and Death. Persona 4 was Joy and Truth. In Persona 5 the main themes seem to be Anger and Freedom (or lack thereof). The main cast of the story are all individuals that have been wronged in some way, and the main focus is of them doing what they can to make life better for themselves and those around them. That is as far as I can go without going into the nitty gritty and begin spoiling things so I will stop there. For the characters and how they are written there is not much here to say other than its nothing super special. Nothing ground breaking or mega original here as you can make a lot of parallels between these characters and characters from past games. I would not be surprised that come February 2017 when this comes out for the rest of the world, the phrase “X character is just Y character from Persona Z” will become very popular. That said, it is quite easy to describe every character as some sort of simple archetype. The bro, the artist, the shut in, the mascot, etc. The great thing about persona though is that these archetypes become more than what they are initially. You spend a year of in game time to get to know and grow with these characters, which makes them special to the player. One problem that might be apparent is that some party members are introduced too late a la Naoto in Persona 4. Where there simply was not enough time to really get to know a character as they arrived so late to the party. The story itself is not terribly complex. Even in my elementary understanding of the Japanese language I could foresee most of the twist and turns of the plot before they happen. This is not a knock on the story as the way that it is delivered to the player. It is by no means bad, but it is definitely no masterpiece for the ages. It had its targets and they hit them pretty spot on rather than trying to do too much or trying too hard and falling flat. Final Thoughts Persona 5 is a great game. Any lover of classic turn based JRPGs will most certainly want to play this game. That said, the other half of the game, involves the plot which may not be for everyone. When you play Persona 5 you are playing a very sleek and rewarding Dungeon crawler that also comes with a “life simulator” which is considerably slower. Depending on how strongly you feel against playing as a group of Japanese teenagers on a day to day basis, you may want to power through those parts or even skip this game entirely. This game is a very solid gameplay experience that plays it safe with its story. Thanks for reading all the way through! I hope this helped you make an informed decision on whether you want to get this game or not. -Prinny_Raider

author: Bkstunt_31
review_title: Let's add a bit of style to our RPGs!
review_text: Well, Persona 5 sure took its time to come out! As a series, Persona is rather well known for blending rather standard JRPG mechanics with its high-school sim game play (ever since Persona 3 re-invited this spin-off series anyways), which found a faithful audience. Still though, Persona 4 came out for the PS2 in 2008. Granted, it had a re-release on the Vita in 2012, but that's still five-plus years between releases! For the most part, Persona 5 delivers exactly what you'd expect from a Persona game, and if you're already a fan of the series picking up this game is definitely a no-brainer (what, do you want to wait another 5-10 years for Persona 6?). If you haven't played this series though, and want to know exactly what Persona 5 is all about, you are in the right place! After nearly 200 hours with the game, I'm ready to go in-depth on what you can expect! Let's do this! We're going to steal your heart... (Story) Like many RPG's you take on the role of an un-named (and mute) protagonist, who is sent to live with a family friend in Tokyo after trying to stop a drunk (but prominent) businessman from forcing himself on a woman late at night. As we all know, life can be unfair, and despite your character trying to do the right thing you are instead charged with assault and are expelled from your old school. Lovely. Thankfully, you are given a second chance to attend high school in Tokyo ("Shujin Academy"), and are now the "new kid" in school but known as a troublemaker (you are on probation, after all). Even your new guardian isn't exactly happy with the situation, forcing you to live in an attic above his coffee shop. Being a Persona game though, soon after moving to a new city and school, our protagonist gets drawn into the "Velvet Room" and discovers he has the ability to enter corrupt individual's "Mind Palaces" and force them to change by stealing their heart. Quite a weird power, granted, but when confronted with a corrupt gym teacher at his new school who is clearly abusing his power and appears to be sexually harassing various female students... well... it's time to put this new power to use... As you can probably tell, this game's story is a wild ride. Being able to forcefully change people's wills is in itself a touchy subject, and definitely a fantastical power. Along the way you'll meet a wide variety of allies who join you. Given that the story takes place over nearly a year (with you playing though almost every single day), your bond with your comrades plays into the story quite a bit (and is one of the biggest selling points story-wise to me personally, as you just spend so much time with your friends). I also really enjoyed the targets that your team decides to use their powers on in this title, as the themes of corruption really hit home in today's world (sexual harassment, people in authority abusing their power, etc...). While the game's main story is undoubtedly a wild ride, I feel that one of the big reasons Persona 5's story as a whole stands out is all of the "off time" you get between the bigger plot progression moments. For example, you will basically progress the main plot every month or so that passes (sometimes longer than that...), but in the meantime you are literally just an ordinary high-school student. So most days you'll go to class and will then have to choose what to do with your time afterwards. This is where the story shines. Perhaps you'll spend your time hanging out with your school friends, and learn more about their past (developing a deeper bond with them). Or maybe you'll volunteer to help a local politician out and learn from his life lessons. Or perhaps you'll hang out with a shady back-street doctor and help her with her experiments while learning how she was ostracized from the field of medicine. Your time is yours to delve into so many relationships with people and discover so many smaller side-stories. You could also just not do any of that and spend your time studying, or going to the gym, or just watching movies.
