My favorite is the Ring of Vanity, an item that not only removes your Personas weaknesses but also grants you the ability to use a barrier that absorbs any attack except almighty once, this came in handy a ton when fighting this game's many secret bosses and even some of the DLC exclusive bosses, more on that later. The palaces were a super great addition and in my opinion the series best dungeons. While the randomized nature of Tartarus is nice, the rarity of savepoints in later sections and bosses that almost require a specific strategy to beat sucked. My only real issue with the palaces is that I don't enjoy one of them, if you've played the game you know exactly the one I'm talking about. During my Joker-only run, it was more bearable because I had grinded to level 99 extremely early in the game so I was able to instakill just about every enemy, even though at that point my builds weren't exactly the best. I will say though, that Palace boss did give me a lot of trouble whereas the ones prior were a breeze. In total there are 10 palaces including the post-game, with my favorites being Palaces 1, 2, 4, 6, and 10. Overall the Palaces are great and I hope the devs stick with this approach to their story dungeons since even now, after 5 total playthroughs of the vanilla dungeons I still enjoy them. Social Links 9.5/10: Persona 5 Royal without a doubt to me does its social links the best, though this time they've been renamed to "Confidants" due to the narrative. But for the sake of consistency, I'll refer to them as social links in this review. For me, there's not a single social link in this game that I dislike or hate. I think they're all done well and do add a lot of emotional weight to some of the characters just like previous games. My only issue is that a bunch of them have this trend where you reach a certain point with them, then the social link gets put on hold until you complete a request in Mementos. This gets annoying since you have to then spend even more time doing the request before moving forward. Aside from that, there's a lot of good, a few amazing, and some mediocre. The ones I felt were the worst were Devil, Tower, Fortune, and Moon. That's not to say they're bad though, they are good, but are outshined by many of the other social links in the game since these don't do much. My favorites however were Justice, Hermit, Councillor, Hierophant, Death, Emperor, and Sun. All of these were extremely good and the character arcs that came with them were super great with a couple of exceptions where the character arcs were more affected by the story rather than the social links with an honorable mention to Faith, despite that character being heavily under-utilized. More on that later. On top of this, each of these provides you with a pretty nice benefit with the only useless feeling abilities being the ones that Devil gives you, they aren't helpful in many situations and while I could see an argument made for them being good, they're not as useful as just about any other social link ability in the game. Social links in this game felt very impactful and hit pretty hard, for the most part, accompanied by this game's excellent soundtrack and the parts that are voiced which help add to the impact of the social links. Now then, lets talk about the Phantom Thieves. The Phantom Thieves 9/10: So thankfully because each member has a codename I can refer to them as such to avoid spoiling who specifically they are. Anyways, the Phantom Thieves are quite the cast of characters, very much a bunch of misfits that all have something in common with each other, that being the ability to summon a Persona. The Phantom Thieves all have a unique role on the team that they represent in the heist genre as well as when it comes to their combat specialties, let's talk about it. Joker, the player character, and the leader. A show-off with style and grace as well as the jack of all trades thanks to his ability to wield the wild card allowing him to use multiple Personas and allowing him to switch between them as he pleases. Mona, the mentor, and healer. Skull, the muscle, and powerhouse. Panther, the femme fatale and flex. Fox, is a refined artist with an eye for quality. Queen, the advisor, strategist, and intelligence. Oracle, the hacker, and all-seeing eye. Noir, is the inside woman that knows exactly how to talk to the targets. Crow, the inside man, and lastly Violet, the acrobat. Each of these characters comes in at a key point in the story and for the most part, they're well developed, but in my opinion, while I do love the Phantom Thieves they aren't as good as our previous teams. A couple of characters are sorely underdeveloped and one is highly underutilized, that being Violet. Without spoilers, I can't say much but from the trailers and everything it seemed like she was going to be an integral part of the story and character you get on the team at the start but that isn't the case. She's only used for one palace and her development is rather rushed compared to the others, while I do like the character the way the developers handled here was pretty poor. Regardless the Phantom Thieves don't deal with the problem that none of them hang out. While I would argue not all of them hang out, some of them do and the chemistry and the way they bounce off each other does feel natural. However, I would argue that either Persona 3 does it better with 4 doing it slightly better than 5. This is however improved in the sequel to 5 Royal, Strikers where the team has been friends for a long time at that point nothing feels awkward. The Phantom Thieves are a fun group that has at least one member anyone can relate to. With that said, they are probably my second favorite team out of the 3 - 4 - 5 trilogy of games, I like their designs, their costumes, their persona designs, and their personalities. They all have their moment and while some aren't utilized as much as they should've been they all serve their purpose well and are a team worthy of your time. My favorites are Crow, Oracle, Fox, and Skull. Story and Themes 8.5/10: The story starts a bit similar to Persona 4 Golden, except this time we've been charged with a crime we didn't commit, assault. The first person we meet is Sojiro Sakura, a cafe owner in roughly his late 40's. He'll be our guardian for the next year and he tells us not to get into any kind of trouble because if we do, it'll be on us and he'll make our lives hell. Unfortunately for us, trouble finds us a couple of days later when we accidentally wandered into the metaverse during our first day of school. This kicks off the events of Persona 5 Royal with its two primary themes, one being a theme during the base game, and the other being the theme overall and for the post-game. The first theme is rebellion, and while the Phantom Thieves may be thieves they aren't bad people, they're very similar to Robin Hood as their goal is to help other people instead of themselves. The other theme is our hardships are what shape us. These themes are very important to the story and it becomes very clear very fast why that is. There is also another theme "unconscious desire" which has been a big part of the 3 - 4 - 5 trilogy. Each game tackling it differently and having the final boss be a physical representation of that, that is no different here. Each character in the game has their reason for rebelling whether it's refusing to believe lies or being sick of being used by everyone to get what the people around them want and not what they want. None of it feels forced either it all makes a lot of sense. The story does lack in multiple places and certainly could be better though it is still good. My main issues are that a couple of parts feel very forced and are there just to create drama for the sake of drama and trying to move the plot forward rather forcefully, and the fact that as mentioned before, Violet is heavily underutilized in this game despite being a new character added with Royal, however, the other new character Dr. Maruki is used sparingly and is a very positive force for the Phantom Thieves to be around giving them an adult they can trust as well as being a very likable character. Overall while Persona 5 Royal isn't as good as the previous two games when it comes to the narrative, the theme of Hardship is my favorite in the series and it's handled extremely well here while also posing a pose an interesting question. We'll talk about that more towards the end of the review since it's more related to the postgame. Overall while the story is the worst of the newer games it's still good, it just needed more work in certain areas, had they done that it would've been a 10 in my opinion. Mementos 8/10: Mementos is Tartarus but going down instead of up. But don't worry because as I mentioned before this isn't where the majority of your time fighting is going to be, that's in the Palaces. Mementos is done quite well and ties into the story in really big ways that you can pick up on pretty early if you know what to look out for. Not only that but it's actually where you go to complete your requests that you receive from characters in the game. Completing said requests will net you a wide variety of awards from weapons, to armor, to accessories, but no costumes. Doing some of these requests as I mentioned before is also a requirement to complete some social links. Mementos is the subway in the Metaverse, except it looks relatively normal when compared to the Palaces and their real-life counterparts. On top of being where you do your requests, Mementos is also where all of the secret bosses are located, however only one of them can be fought on New Game, the other two can only be fought in NG+. This is where you can also find the Reaper, a returning mini-boss from the previous two games. Mementos is also a great spot to grind for EXP, Yen, and loot. I don't have much to say on Mementos aside from it being vastly superior to Tartarus, minus the music, the music for Mementos isn't as good compared to Tartarus chunks 2, 4, 5, and 6 in my personal opinion. It's also helped by the fact that it is only 1/4 the size of Tartarus without including Monad which does make it feel a lot less repetitive than Tartarus. All in all, during my playthrough of 5 I didn't like it, but while playing Royal I did begin to appreciate it and enjoy it quite a bit and I do think it's a massive step up to Persona 3's Tartarus since the two are extremely similar. Villains 7.5/10: Good news, Persona 5 Royal has multiple villains! Bad news, some of them aren't that good. The first villain is extremely good and hateable, really just a disgusting scummy piece of crap, and then the second villain is fairly good and one I enjoyed, but the next couple after that take a dip in quality, with the last technically 3 villains being good. Persona 5 Royal's base game is a perfect example of quantity does not equal quality. Had we spent more time with the second villain and the second to last, the one who steers a ship it would've been better. Except unlike Persona 3, the villains do something and have some motivation as we get to go into their psyche and learn more about them. I think the game also does benefit from having multiple villains, though I think it could've been toned down to 3 or 4 and they would've been much better. Regardless I think they are the worst part of the base game but things could certainly be worse, they could be Strega. Royal Post-game 9/10 - Villain 10/10 - Palace 9.5/10: Finally, I get to talk about the post-game. The post-game adds around a good 30 hours to the original game. But instead of just being an extended epilogue or some additional story content where it's 97% gameplay, the postgame is more of the same, but with a twist. Now, I can barely even say anything about the story because this IS after, but what I can say is that not everything is how it should be, some things are rather.. off. The main theme of the postgame is hardships. That's all I'm saying. But it does include a bonus palace, a new party member, one of my favorite video game villains ever, and some excellent new music. This last portion of the game also has two completely different endings, of which Atlus is not outwardly confirming as canon. However, if you've played Persona 4 Golden you should have a good idea for which one is canon, and based on how one of them ends. The new palace is also different from the rest and doesn't pose a challenge but that isn't necessarily the point of it, it's not supposed to be very difficult perse more something that makes you think and wants your attention and for you to pay attention to every little detail. It's almost as if it's asking you a question directly. There is a ton of symbolism from the colors, to the puzzles, and is heavily inspired by some of the depictions in the Christian bible and even some of H.P. Lovecraft's work. I'll leave it at that because I don't want to give away too much. Personally, for me, this is my favorite palace in the game with my ONLY gripe being that it absolutely could've been more difficult to get through. I do love the post-game and if it went on for even longer I would've loved that. The fact that it doesn't does suck and the fact that when the game ends you can't go back and replay palaces or anything is something that does bother me and I hope Persona 6 does take a page from Strikers and add that feature in, even though Strikers was made in collaboration with a different developer while being more gameplay focused and is vastly different from the mainline Persona games. Bonus content: So this game has some bonus content included in Royal that was originally DLC for 5. It's just a bunch of challenge fights that give you a bunch of rewards, however, there are a couple of special fights. The first one is against Makoto Yuki, the leader of S.E.E.S. and the playable main character in Persona 3. The other is against Yu Narukami, the leader of the Investigation Team and playable main character from Persona 4. These fights are super cool because each uses a set of Personas that Atlus seems to have deemed as their canon teams. They also use Mass Destruction and Reach Out To The Truth as the boss music is super cool. There are 2 versions of these fights, a level 50 fight, and a level ??? (99) fight. The level 50 challenge is a decent challenge and doesn't require the most optimized builds by any means, however, the level ??? fights do if you want to reach the max score and get the best rewards. Honestly, these are just a great bit of fan service and are enjoyable and they give you some nice rewards for your efforts. Thieves Den: Thieves Den? What's that? Well, I'm glad you asked! it's cool actually. So the Thieves Den does sort of canonically exist as it's described by one of the new characters, Jose, who does not have a social link nor is he a part of any team. He plays a very minor role and does imply some interesting things, we'll talk about that in our next section. Anyways so the Thieves Den is your palace, a place where you can relax, buy concept art, cutscenes, music, and other things using points you earned for completing goals the game has set for you. I love that Atlus added this because there is a lot to unlock here and there's a ton of concept art in here and if you're like me and a huge fan of that type of stuff you'll enjoy the Thieves Den. Also completing the Thieves Den's objectives gives you two items. One is an item that makes it so you can summon registered Persona from the compendium free of charge. The other is an accessory that makes you completely invisible to shadows in a palace. I actually just fully completed it during my last playthrough and trust me, some objectives you'll have to work for but it's worth it in the end especially if you're working on Persona builds, it allows you to spend your money on other things and saves you a ton of money in the long run. If anything is brought back in Persona 6 I do hope it's this and I get the feeling they probably will, or maybe some form of it, like customizing where you live. Implications for Persona 6: Based on what Jose says and the way the plot moves, Persona 6 is going to be a very different game and with a former Velvet Attendant making moves in Ultimax and possibly behind the scenes in Persona 5 Royal. This is also probably going to be the case because Igor's Japanese voice actor Isamu Tanonaka, passed away in 2010 and Atlus was able to work around this in Persona 5 but it is highly unlikely he will return out of respect and other story-related things. With this year's string of announcements, I wouldn't be surprised if Atlus reveals Persona 6 while also showing us who will take Igor's role as the master of the Velvet Room, and I have my theory on who that may be. On top of that Persona, 6's director as of now has not been announced. As well as certain events that transpire in Royal 6 could very well reference Persona 5 more than previous games have with their predecessor since said events did have a lot of implications yet we only got a small peephole into what happened when it seemed to be implied that things went far further than we were shown. For now, all we can do is theorize but I do suspect things might feel a bit more SMT-ish in Persona 6 than in previous games. Conclusion: Now, this 10/10 does not mean it's perfect, the game is flawed and no game out there is without flaws, but a 10/10 for me is a game that stands above the rest as something special, something unique that I believe everybody should give a shot. The only other 2 games that I played I felt were 10/10's were Bloodborne and Nier Automata. My love for Persona 5 Royal matches Bloodborne, I could almost say either one is my favorite, however, Bloodborne feels like a game that was made for me. I would love to do a review on that game, however, going back to it now when even on the PS5 it's locked at 30fps is hard to do. Persona 5 Royal is a game that in all honesty did change my life a bit, it taught me a lot and opened my eyes to many things and is part of the reason I got into anime last year. Something about Persona 5 Royal just hooked me like no other game has, except Bloodborne. I love this game with all my heart and it's truly a game I can recommend to anyone. It has a lot going for it and I think just about anyone can play it and will find something to love about it. From the combat to the music, to the Phantom Thieves, to the villains, and so much more I love this game and I truly believe it's worthy of being called one of the best games ever made. But that's my opinion and there are plenty of people out there who would disagree with me. This game made me laugh, and it made me cry. It made me feel sad, it made me feel hopeless, and it made me feel so much more. This game is quite the ride and one I will never in my life forget. I don't know what else I have to say to convince you but please, give this one a shot and at least complete that first palace because I promise you, it'll be worth it.

author: TrailsOfPersona
review_title: Royalty That Lives On
review_text: Persona 5 was already one of the greatest games ever made when it was released as a base game. When they announced the release of Royal with a few new characters and more content, I thought they could only ruin it. It was such a perfectly crafted story paced so well that the thought of any addition had to have been awkwardly forced in. I felt the new characters would have been force fed and added nothing. After all, while I certainly wouldn't say the new content in Persona 4 Golden ruined Persona 4 to any degree, I don't think much there added anything too interesting to the story. Most of what was added in Persona 4 Golden was useless but harmless. Even before that, I don't think the addition of The Answer in Persona 3 FES was a slam dunk either. Better than the additions of Golden for sure, but not outstanding. I was entirely wrong, fortunately. Everything added in Royal improved it. Yoshizawa became my favorite character in the franchise (if my avatar didn't make that an easy call to make.) But more on her later. Since I won't be doing a review on the base game, I will add my thoughts on what is shared by both. The graphics are so amazingly stylish. To say the look of the game is entirely of its own would be an understatement. It has a look that is unmatched and unrivaled. And the music is even better. The music is easily in contention for best game OST of all time. The mix of funk, metal, pop, and even a tiny bit of jazz is technically wonderful and also fits every mode it needs. Peaceful and serene, heavy and bombastic, dark and moody? It does it all. The Whims of Fate, Price, and Rivers in the Desert are my favorites, with an honorable mention to Gentle Madman, which is a new track for Royal that is cold, beautiful, and perfectly fitting for the dungeon it takes place in. Combat is addicting and stimulating turn-based style. Two new elements are added in Persona 5, and I'm not quite sure how needed they were. It kind of just makes more the MC has to be relied on for in my opinion, which taxes him a bit more. Combat is also unquestionably easier than the two prior modern Persona games. I wouldn't call Persona 5 an easy game, but if you are used to older Persona games or SMT titles, it will be strikingly easier. For those new to the series, it will provide a decent challenge without being too frustrating. One thing I really did not like about Persona 5's combat is how there are no unique enemies anymore. Every enemy has the ability to become a Persona. In Persona 3 and 4, enemies were unique. They weren't 'recruitable' like they are here. It gave Shadows originality, where enemies here just feel like repurposed Personas. The story of Persona 5 was brilliantly executed. It is a story that hit young adults around the time it came out right through the heart. The story of the previous generation ruining the future of the younger generation while they have little ability to fight back is one I think every person who was in their late teens to early 20's at the time of release felt strongly about. The Phantom Thieves gave that audience an escape where they could fight back. Fictional or not, it really was catharsis for so many. And even now when the most concentrated of that segment might be gone, it is still a story that is extremely relatable. It is paced quite well, and though predictable in some places, it has enough cool twists and turn to keep you hooked to keep playing it. I wouldn't say the story is QUITE as good as Persona 3's, but it's very close. And it easily blows Persona 4's out of the water. Beyond combat, though, Persona 5 also has the social link aspect. The swap between social links and combat is part of what makes Persona as a series so addicting. If you start to get bored of one aspect, you just do the other. The social links in Persona 5 are quite well done. It was really nice to see that the majority of your non party member social links aren't just classmates like in the last two games. Joker's social links are from vastly different walks of life and really make him feel like his title. A Joker. He is able to take all of these different people with different skills and backgrounds and add what they have to offer to his arsenal. Social links are extremely well done. My one complaint is that they fell into the same trap as Persona 4 with social links that Persona 3 did not have. The point of social links is to mix them up with combat so nothing gets boring. But if you want to play the game optimally, you are encouraged to do the dungeons as fast as possible. So that means with every dungeon, you ideally want to do all of your dungeon and combat immediately, and then focus on social links once those are done. The way they made the game kind of makes it go against intended purposes. Character depth and growth on the other hand is where Persona 5 falters a bit. The characters still aren't poorly done, but the ball bounces a few times before being caught. Most of the characters only really have much in the way of growth and development around their recruitment time, and don't do much more beyond that. Ryuji stays pretty one dimensional the entire time. He learns a bit of patience and the importance of friends, but little else. Ann was the biggest dropped ball. She is put between a rock and a hard place and faces some very, very hard trauma during her introductory arc. But when that arc is over, she becomes a pretty one-note character that seemingly overcomes the trauma at the drop of a hat. There was a lot more about Ann that could have been expanded upon and explored. Haru is an absolute sweetheart who I wish they did more with. She joins AFTER the halfway point of the original game and has very little screen time. After her arc, she is not focused on again outside of her social link. She almost feels like a last minute addition to the cast. Now, I'm not going to go paragraph after paragraph analyzing every single character. Certain characters ARE done better like Morgana and Makoto, but the cast, as a whole, leaves a little to be desired in terms of their growth and improvement through the course of the game. My favorite in the original game was Futaba. She doesn't have quite the development of Morgana or Makoto, but her struggles with mental health and strength of character to fight from being a shut in to really overcoming her Mother's death and realizing the importance of having close people was really inspiring. She goes from being a truly frightened and traumatized girl to an incredibly strong young woman taking her independence back. I still adore Futaba! But when Royal was released, in came Yoshizawa. Yoshizawa deserves a paragraph of her own. I WILL be talking about spoilers. So if you haven't played Royal and want to without being spoiled, skip this paragraph. Yoshizawa is introduced and is immediately an immensely kind, polite, respectful young woman with a competitive spirit and belly full of fire. She seemingly has her own trauma that she has mostly overcome. ...Or so you think. In truth, Yoshizawa has been utterly broken by survivor's guilt. A topic not covered by many games. Her sister died saving her, and she feels her sister had value and she does not. So she mentally became her sister to not break mentally. Through the course of the game, you help her accept her survivor's guilt and come to terms with the fact that it isn't her fault her sister died, and that she isn't worthless. Her struggles and growth are heart-wrenching. She is also a perfect foil for Joker. They both inspire each other and push the other to keep fighting. The only thing about Yoshizawa is that the developers were put between the hammer and the anvil when it came to adding her to the story. If they added her to previous dungeons and storylines and she WASN'T a well received character, fans might have burned her at the stake and claimed she ruined Royal. So what they did was keep her as a side character until the final brand new dungeon. Instead what happened is the opposite of what they feared. She was a huge hit as a character and most gamer's complain they don't have her longer than that. For those of you who feel that way and play on PC, I will just say modding is your friend! The new antagonist of Royal is also one that makes you feel conflicted. He has great ideas but just isn't going about trying to enact them in good ways. They try to keep him somewhat of a secret but...it should be pretty obvious who it is to most gamers. He is a fitting villain for the new additions to the storyline, but at the same time, he doesn't command nearly the same fear or omnipresent looming threat that Yaldabaoth had from the original. I sort of felt like he was a slight step down from Yaldabaoth in terms of threat. All of the new other elements in Royal are also amazing. The card game Tycoon is just as addicting as the gameplay. I've sunk tons of hours into Tycoon. The dart minigame is fun and has cool benefits, and the jazz club also is a fantastic way to spend your time late game when you've done most social links. Persona 3 will likely always be my favorite game in the Persona franchise, but Persona 5 far surpasses 4 for me. And Royal only made it better. There is very, very little Persona 5 doesn't do well, and what it doesn't are generally pretty small things that can be looked past. I know for many of us gamers, when a game gets insane hype, it's hard to try and play games like that. For fear of a game not living up to that hype or for fear of a game just getting hype through mob mentality. I completely understand that. As someone who understands that, I STILL will firmly encourage you to play Persona 5. I certainly won't guarantee you come out thinking it is a 10/10 experience like me, but I can promise you will have a good time with it and find value in the story it tells. Persona 5 Royal is genuinely a generational game. Games like this are not ones that come out often. And I don't say things like that lightly. It is truly and easily one of the greatest games of all time to me. There is nothing like it.

author: Galactus21
review_title: More Persona 5? Yes, please!
review_text: The original Persona 5 was one of my favorite games during this console generation. I was ecstatic when Persona 5 Royal was announced for the PlayStation 4. After spending the last few weeks playing through the game and its new content, I can safely say that Persona 5 is as fun as it ever was. Packed with some new characters and content, this version is well worth spending money on and playing through again. Persona 5 Royal, like the original, is a fantastic Japanese RPG filled with memorable characters, good storyline, and great game play. Persona 5 follows a group of high school students, forming a group called the Phantom Thieves. Joker, the main protagonist and the leader of the Phantom Thieves, is a student who was wrongly accused of a crime. As punishment he is banished to Tokyo to live in the care of a guardian and go to a new school. Over time, he meets other students who share an ability to enter cognitive worlds of criminals and change their hearts. A big part of Persona 5 is your ability to build relationships with your team members and other in game characters. Spending time with them will increase your rankings with these characters. The story arcs around these character interactions really rally you around their character and the overall story. You bond with the characters over time, as you see them grow through out the game. During these interactions, you will have different options that you can choose to respond to these characters. Depending on what you choose, you can earn points towards the next ranking. The game’s story is also one of its strong points and is presented through a series of cut scenes, dialogue, and character interactions. The story is coherent and keeps you engage. The story revolves going into palaces of criminals. These palaces are essentially cognitive worlds, where that criminal’s twisted desires are in full display. Stealing their treasure, leads to their confession of the crimes they’ve committed. As you progress, you’ll find out additional details about this cognitive world. The way the story is presented is engaging and fun to follow. From a game play perspective, Persona 5 Royal features a turn base combat system. Growing up I really enjoyed that classic turn base combat system. Over the years, this type of combat fell out of favor. Just like the original, I enjoyed the turn base combat that the game utilizes. During your combat, you have different types of attacks available to you. You have melee attacks, gun attacks, and persona attacks. Melee and guns do not use any SP, but gun attacks are limited to certain number of bullets per battle. Persona attacks are essentially magic attacks, where you can heal, cast fire attacks, and so forth. Different types of enemies have different weaknesses, where you can essentially knock them down. Vice versa, some enemies will have resistance to certain attacks. If all enemies have been hit with attacks that they are weak against, they will all be knocked down, which then allows for a collective attack from your team members to deal large amounts of damage. When you successfully knock down an enemy, you can perform an additional attack or perform a baton pass. A baton pass allows you to give that turn to another team member. That way if you have enemies weak against ice and fire attacks, you can enlist two team members with those attacks. A new type of attack in Persona 5 Royal is the showtime attack. These are tag team attacks that deal large amounts of damage. They are also quite cool to look at, as the attack showcases some cool scenes. As you progress through the game, different team members will come up with these showtime attacks. For example, there is one between Ryuji and Makoto. There is one for Yusuke and Ann. These are fun to utilize and help reinforce that energetic feel that Persona 5 seems to have. The game’s voice acting, and music is also another strong point. The voice acting for majority of the characters was well done. The newer characters like Kasumi and Maruki were also solid. The musical soundtrack was also catchy. Persona 5 Royal’s art style was also splendidly done, and I really enjoyed the direction there. Certain scenes during the game feels like an anime. Character models also look great. The game also ran smooth. The production values were topnotch throughout. Persona 5 Royal, like the original Persona 5, has a lot to love. Everything from the story and characters to the combat was well made. The final product was simply a fantastic game, where I found myself completely immersed for over a hundred hours. The game is one of the better games during this console generation and playing through it again just helps reinforce that. Even if you played the original, I would still wholeheartedly recommend Royal. Persona 5 Royal has more content and still retains that charm that made the original great.

author: Johnalove
review_title: Refining a Masterpiece
review_text: Persona 5 was my introduction to the JRPG genre and it quickly became my favorite videogame of all time; I remember starting a New Game+ playthrough literally the day after finishing my first playthrough because I had already missed it. Persona 5 Royal was my most anticipated videogame for some time, so I decided to preorder the Ultimate Edition... was it worth? Narrative : Persona 5's story is one of my favorites because I love the themes of rebellion, justice and human cognition, and the development of its characters. In Royal, the story remains mostly the same, but it's been expanded with 2 additional characters, a new Palace and a third semester, which is undoubtedly the best story arc in the entire game. Gameplay : Persona 5 plays like a typical turn based JRPG with a wide variety of skills, elements, status effects and items, however, the unique mechanics (e.g. Baton pass), the flashy animations and the wonderful user interface make the combat system very smooth and impressive. Royal's combat system is the same, the gameplay is improved in almost every way; there are new major mechanics like the grappling hook and the showtimes but there are also minor improvements over the baton pass and the guns, which made the combat system even more fun. Characters : Same with the characters; in Persona 5 Royal, not only there are 3 additional characters, but there's also a reworked confidant and a new arc for a vital character as well. Improvements/Changes : The Palaces have received some changes; there are new areas to explore, new items to collect and the most frustrating parts have been removed. The music is even better; Shoji Meguro strikes again with a unique "Royal" touch this time. Lastly, there are new additions for Mementos, interesting changes to the boss battles, more free time and side-content, a ton of other QoL improvements and even faster loading times. Flaws : Unfortunately though, while the story of the game got better, the pacing is still slightly inconsistent at times. Other than that... what more could I ask for? Pros : Expanded story Refined gameplay Additional characters Major improvements Minor tweaks More content Cons : Balancing issues Final Rating : 10/10 Persona 5 Royal is Persona 5 at its finest; by improving upon the original game in every way while adding features that I consider essential to be in the game, it managed to exceed my high expectations. Persona 5 was already an RPG masterpiece, and Persona 5 Royal is a significantly better experience overall; it's undoubtedly one of the best videogames ever made. Do I recommend it? : If you've played Persona 5 before, I'd say yes, however, I wouldn't recommend buying Royal at full price unless you're a big fan of the original release because it's not a completely different game. If you haven't played Persona 5 before, then it's a must play, especially if you enjoy playing JRPGs because Persona 5 Royal is one of the best games you will ever play.

author: RealScrapz
review_title: Probably the closest we have ever gotten to perfect in a game
review_text: When Persona 5 came to Xbox Game Pass 4 months ago, I decided to give it a shot. Now its my favorite game. Gameplay The game is a turn based JRPG that excels in everything it tries to be. The main gameplay loop consists of learning enemy weaknesses and then striking them to chain attacks, or alternatively, pass the attack to a teammate for bonus damage. This is made possible due to your party members having their own persona, which allows them to use magic skills that consume SP, or physical skills that consume HP. The character you play as has access to multiple personas, which allows for endless amounts of strategy and build variety. You also have the option to use a gun in battle, which has one magazine you can use for that fight and replenishes ammo automatically when you reach the next battle. Outside of battles, you explore the distorted realities of criminals in order to force them to turn themselves in. The design of these realities ranges from a perverted volleyball coach's school appearing as a castle, to a corrupt CEO's workplace appearing as a robotic sweatshop in outer space. Exploring these levels will keep you hooked if the battle system hadn't already. These levels also have puzzles that test your knowledge, or in some cases, your sanity. Outside of your dungeon crawling shenanigans, you live the life of a Japanese high schooler, instead of choosing to spend time exploring levels, you can make friends to get abilities for fighting, go to the gym to increase HP and SP, and many more options. There are not many limitations on where you can go in the real world, and everywhere you go has at least some benefit, whether it be money, items, or bonus stats. Story I won't go too in depth with the story to avoid spoiler reasons, but this games story is as good as the gameplay, maybe even better. The game begins with the protagonist escaping a giant casino. This segment throws you into a battle pretty quickly, shows off the amazing animation, and has some of the best video game music ever made playing while all this happens. This segment shows the player how stylish and chaotic this game is going to be throughout it's entirety. The protagonist fails to escape the casino and gets captured. He is then interrogated, and then you get a flashback from around 8 months prior, starting the game. Most of the game being told through flashbacks worked wonders for this game and it's story. One of the things this aspect adds is whenever you start a new friendship, the game suddenly goes back to the present and the person interrogating you questions you about the person you became friends with. One of the few problems I have with this game is that after this part of the game, it becomes really slow for a few hours, turning away new players who might not have as much patience as me. Another problem with this section is that it refuses to tell you where you are supposed to go in important segments where you are exploring the real world areas for the first time. One of my friends became stuck because he could not find the third year volley ball player. Other Positives The music in this game is fantastic, every song fits pretty well where its used. You have songs like Rivers in The Desert which are great for the late game bosses, Tokyo Emergency which is probably the one thing that could convince me to go outside and touch grass, and the second version of price which gives me payday vibes. There is a reason I have so many persona songs in my music playlist, I highly encourage you to listen to this game's ost (don't read the comments if you are on youtube, there are likely spoilers). This game's UI is extremely creative while also not being overcomplicated. The pause menu is filled to the brim with style. When you go to the weapons shop it only gets better. Persona 5 Royal also has a lot of convenience, there is an area in the game called "Mementos" where you can explore randomly generated floors to search for items and grind enemies for levels. Another convenient aspect in the game is that it gives you lots of time to do stuff you want to do, you have from 4/8 to 12/23 (or 2/2 if you go for the secret ending) to do everything you need. Conclusion Anyways, you can see now that this game is extremely well made and is 100% worth playing. I hope you enjoyed reading my review and I also hope you enjoy playing Persona 5 Royal.
